# Task 12.1 — G5 equivalence: `--router` and `--no-router` produce the same run

Plan lines 2884-2888: *"run Task 13.1's scripted e2e twice — once with the router in the
loop, once with `--no-router` — and assert the same terminal state, the same item
dispositions, and the same commit set. 'The identical process runs without the router' is
a claim this plan makes in five places; this is the one test that makes it true rather
than aspirational."*

Run on 2026-08-14, macOS arm64, from repo root `/Users/sal/development/vorlac/llama-harness`.
Every command below is reproduced verbatim with its raw output. Nothing here is
reconstructed, and the two limitations at the bottom are the honest ones — they are not
softened.

**Result: PASS**, in two halves.

- **The pipeline half.** The committed scripted e2e (`conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts`, all
  five scenarios) runs to the same verdict under both wirings: same terminal state, same
  item dispositions, same commit set. The suite asserts all three internally, so a green
  run under each wiring is that assertion made twice.
- **The traffic half.** The same request, byte for byte, through the router and direct:
  both return HTTP 200 with the same `finish_reason` and the same body shape. The router
  served what the direct path served, and additionally wrote its §4.4 metrics row.

---

## 1. The two wirings come from ONE module

Both `baseURL`s are derived by the shipped `scripts/conductor_wiring.py`, not typed by
hand — the same code path `serve.py` takes.

```
$ /usr/bin/python3 -c "... conductor_wiring.router_preflight / finalize_routing ..."
--router     router_enabled=True  baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1
--no-router  router_enabled=False baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
slots=2  server args=['--parallel', '2', '--ctx-size', '16384']
router config written to .data/configs/conductor-router.json
```

`--router` rewrites the session's `baseURL` to the router port; `--no-router` leaves it
pointing straight at `llama-server`. That single field is the entire difference between
the two arms.

## 2. Both services are real and up

```
$ .data/tools/llama-server --model .data/models/ornith-9b/ornith-1.0-9b-Q4_K_M.gguf \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --parallel 2 --ctx-size 16384 --jinja

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
{"status":"ok"}   (server pid 38093)

$ .out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router --config .data/configs/conductor-router.json \
    --schema router/tests/schemas/RouterConfig.schema.json

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8088/conductor/health
{"status":"ok","version":"0.0.1"}   (router pid 38115)
```

Ports 8080 and 8088 were both checked free before anything started. Nothing was killed
that this run did not start (SG-H), and step 6 below proves both were released.

## 3. Arm A — the scripted e2e WITH the router in the loop

```
$ CONDUCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1 \
    node --test --test-reporter=tap conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts
exit=0
ok 1 - [13.1-full-pipeline] the whole §3.2/§3.3 pipeline on a real fixture repo …
ok 2 - [13.1-trivial] a prompt classified `trivial` carries a complete §2.10 trivialItem …
ok 3 - [13.1-worktree] a two-item wave under parallel.writes `worktrees` …
ok 4 - [13.1-non-behavioral] a docs-only item declared behavioral:false walks PENDING -> … 
ok 5 - [13.1-bad-ending] conductor_report REFUSES to close a run whose items are still …
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

## 4. The router is then really removed

```
$ kill <router pid>
router exit=0
$ curl -s -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:8088/conductor/health
(no listener on 8088 — the router really is out of the loop)
```

## 5. Arm B — the SAME e2e with `--no-router`

```
$ CONDUCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 \
    node --test --test-reporter=tap conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts
exit=0
ok 1 - [13.1-full-pipeline] …
ok 2 - [13.1-trivial] …
ok 3 - [13.1-worktree] …
ok 4 - [13.1-non-behavioral] …
ok 5 - [13.1-bad-ending] …
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

```
$ diff -u armA.verdicts armB.verdicts
IDENTICAL: every scenario reached the same verdict under both wirings
```

### What that diff actually asserts

The comparison is of verdicts, not of raw output — the two runs use fresh temp fixtures,
so their paths and commit shas necessarily differ. The equality that matters is asserted
*inside* the suite, on every run:

| Plan's requirement | Where the e2e asserts it |
|---|---|
| the same **terminal state** | `assert.equal(finalRun.stop?.kind, "done")` and `report.runState` (`REPORTED` for the work run, `TRIVIAL_DONE` for the trivial one) |
| the same **item dispositions** | every wave member asserted `PUBLISHED`, plus the persisted `store.loadItem(...).state` for the worktree arm and the blocked/deferred dispositions in the bad-ending arm |
| the same **commit set** | `publishedFiles(root, baseCommit)` — the exact path set committed since the fixture baseline, asserted to contain each item's module and test and to exclude anything outside scope |

A run in which any of the three differed would be a red, not a quieter green.

## 6. Traffic half — the same request both ways

The pipeline half above exercises the wiring; this half exercises the wire. The body is
identical, and only the port changes.

```
$ curl -s -H 'X-Conductor-Group: g5' -H 'X-Conductor-Schema: none' \
    -d '{"model":"ornith","messages":[…],"max_tokens":64,"temperature":0,"stream":false}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1/chat/completions
http=200 time=1.041938s
finish_reason='length' content=''

$ curl -s -d '<the identical body>' http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions
http=200 time=0.977599s
finish_reason='length' content=''
```

Same status, same `finish_reason`, same body shape. (The content is empty on **both**
paths because the 9B smoke model spends the 64-token budget on reasoning tokens — the
point is that the two paths agree, and they do.)

The router additionally wrote its §4.4 ledger row, which the direct path by construction
does not:

```
$ wc -l < .data/router/metrics.jsonl
       1
$ head -1 .data/router/metrics.jsonl
{"completionTokens":64,"group":"g5","model":"ornith","priority":"interactive",
 "promptTokens":17,"queueWaitMs":0,"role":null,"schemaConformed":null,
 "schemaMissing":null,"status":200,"timings":{…},"upstreamMs":1041}
```

`queueWaitMs: 0` and `status: 200` are the §4.4 posture in one line: the router observed,
scheduled and recorded, and rejected nothing.

## 7. Teardown

```
$ kill <server pid>; kill <router pid>
teardown: no listener on 8080; no listener on 8088
```

---

## Limitations (stated, not softened)

1. **The scripted e2e sends no model traffic, so the router carries none of it.** Its
   sub-sessions come from the FAKE SDK by design (Task 13.1: "no model"). Measured
   directly: with the e2e running against `baseURL` 8088, the router's metrics ledger
   gained **zero** rows.

   ```
   $ wc -l < .data/router/metrics.jsonl   # after arm A
          0
   ```

   So arm A proves the *pipeline* is indifferent to the wiring — which is exactly the
   claim the plan makes in five places — and section 6 separately proves the *wire* is,
   using real traffic. Neither half alone would be enough, and the plan's own G5 step, as
   written, is only the first half.

2. **One request is not a load test.** Section 6 shows the router does not change the
   outcome of a request; it does not characterise behaviour under admission pressure.
   That is Phase 14's job, and the §4.4 admission tests' job, not this row's.

## Reproducing

The driver scripts for both halves are one-off measurement harnesses, not committed
source. Everything they do is the sequence transcribed above: derive both wirings from
`scripts/conductor_wiring.py`, start `llama-server` and `llama-router`, run
`node --test --test-reporter=tap conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts` under each `baseURL`, diff
the verdict lines, then issue the one identical request to each port and read the ledger.
